document_title: General Awareness & Reasoning Test - Planning, Budgeting, and Government Accounting

questions.question: In which year planning commissions was set up?
questions.explanation: The National Planning Commission (NPC) of Nepal was established in 1956 A.D. (2013 B.S.) to formulate and guide the periodic development plans of the country[cite: 16].

questions.question: When was first five year plan introduced?
questions.explanation: Nepal's very first five-year periodic plan was officially introduced in 2013 B.S. (1956/57 A.D.) to initiate systematic national economic development[cite: 16].

questions.question: Planning Commission of Nepal is a/an
questions.explanation: The National Planning Commission operates primarily as an advisory body to the Government of Nepal for formulating national development policies and periodic plans[cite: 16].

questions.question: The basic objectives of planning of Nepal are: 1. Economic growth 2. Affluent self-reliant 3. Employment generation 4. Population growth
questions.explanation: The foundational objectives of national planning in Nepal target economic growth, self-reliance, and employment generation, whereas population growth is typically a challenge to manage rather than a primary goal of planning[cite: 16].

questions.question: On the basis of Ideology, what kinds of planning is/are adopted in Nepal
questions.explanation: Nepal's socio-economic structure incorporates elements across different frameworks, embracing aspects associated with capitalistic, socialistic, and mixed planning approaches over its modern history[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which of the following criteria for the evaluation of planning deals most with whether the program achieves its goals or not?
questions.explanation: Effectiveness specifically measures the degree to which a program, project, or plan successfully achieves its intended goals and targets[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which of the following is not a factor(s) when classifying a plan on time-frame?
questions.explanation: Plans are classified by time-frame into short-term, medium-term (periodic), long-term, and perspective plans. Inducement planning is an economic governance method, not a time-frame classification[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which one is not the process of planning?
questions.explanation: Mobilization of resources is an implementation and execution phase rather than a core analytical or conceptual step in the foundational planning formulation process[cite: 16].

questions.question: The main responsible body for formulating planning is/are
questions.explanation: National planning involves multiple apex bodies, including the National Planning Commission for drafting, the National Development Council for broad guidance, and the Council of Ministers for final approval[cite: 16].

questions.question: What is the role of medium term expenditure framework (MTEF)?

options.c: To help in establishing tie between planning and budget

questions.explanation: The Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) acts as a vital institutional bridge connecting long-term/periodic national planning with annual budgetary allocations[cite: 16].

questions.question: When was the Mid-term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) implemented in Nepal?
questions.explanation: The MTEF tool was formally introduced and implemented in Nepal starting from the Fiscal Year 2059/60 BS to enhance resource allocation discipline[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which economic system relies heavily on government intervention and centralized planning?
questions.explanation: A command economy is characterized by a centralized government controlling all major aspects of production, distribution, and economic planning[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct? 1. Planning Commission is a constitutional body. 2. The Prime Minister is the Chairman of the Planning Commission.
questions.explanation: The National Planning Commission is a government advisory body, not a constitutional body (making statement 1 false), while the Prime Minister serves as its ex-officio Chairman (making statement 2 correct)[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which of the following Nodal institution for the implementation of sustainable development goals in Nepal?

options.b: Ministry of poverty alleviation & land reforms

questions.explanation: The National Planning Commission (NPC) functions as the central nodal entity responsible for coordinating and monitoring the implementation of Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in Nepal[cite: 16].

questions.question: Who appoints the vice-chairperson of the Planning Commission?
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister, in the capacity of the Chairperson of the National Planning Commission, recommends and appoints its Vice-Chairperson[cite: 16].

questions.question: Who amongst the following is the chairperson of National Planning Commission?
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister of Nepal serves as the ex-officio chairperson of the National Planning Commission[cite: 16].

questions.question: Who is the Chairperson of Steering Committee of Periodic plan?
questions.explanation: The Vice-Chairman (VC) of the National Planning Commission heads the Steering Committee responsible for guiding the formulation of periodic plans[cite: 16].

questions.question: Who will be the ex-officio member of the National Planning Commission of Nepal?
questions.explanation: Key administrative leaders such as the Chief Secretary of the Government of Nepal and the Secretary of the Ministry of Finance serve as ex-officio members of the NPC[cite: 16].

questions.question: From which language did the English word 'Budget' originate?
questions.explanation: The word 'budget' originates from the Old French word 'bougette', meaning a small leather bag or pouch used to store state financial papers[cite: 16].

questions.question: LMBIS is related to?
questions.explanation: Line Ministry Budget Information System (LMBIS) is an electronic web-based system utilized for budget preparation, submission, and management in Nepal[cite: 16].

questions.question: When was the first budget of Nepal presented?
questions.explanation: Nepal's first national budget was presented on Magh 21, 2008 B.S. by then Finance Minister Subarna Shamsher Rana[cite: 16].

questions.question: Who is the first finance minister of Modern Nepal to present budget in Nepal?
questions.explanation: Subarna Shamsher Rana holds the historical distinction of being the first finance minister to present the national budget of modern Nepal in 2008 B.S.[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which of the following is/are the objective(s) of Budget?

options.a: To achieve economic growth, economic stability and economic development
options.b: To implement the plans and programs

questions.explanation: A national budget serves multifaceted objectives: driving economic growth and stability, operationalizing government policies, and ensuring tight financial control[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which one of the following is responsible for the preparation and presentation of federal budget of Nepal?
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Finance holds the primary statutory responsibility for formulating and presenting the annual federal budget to parliament[cite: 16].

questions.question: As the provisional of present constitution of Nepal, when was federal budget of Nepal presented?
questions.explanation: Under the current Constitution of Nepal, the federal government must present its annual budget on Jestha 15 each year[cite: 16].

questions.question: What is the role of the Ministry of Finance in the budget preparation process in Nepal?

options.a: To prepare and present the budget to the parliament
options.b: To implement the budget once it is approved
options.c: To monitor the implementation of the budget throughout the year

questions.explanation: The Ministry of Finance oversees the entire budget lifecycle, including drafting, legislative presentation, implementation oversight, and continuous monitoring[cite: 16].

questions.question: Legal provisions for budgeting in Nepal is /are

options.b: Financial procedure Act, 2055 & Financial procedure Rules 2064

questions.explanation: Budgetary governance in Nepal is governed by constitutional provisions, statutory financial procedure legislation, and administrative guidelines[cite: 16].

questions.question: Budget needs to be approved by;
questions.explanation: Before implementation, the national budget must receive formal statutory approval from the Federal Parliament[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which part of the Constitution of Nepal deals with the Federal Financial Procedures?
questions.explanation: Part 10 of the Constitution of Nepal outlines the legal and procedural framework governing federal financial procedures, including revenue and expenditure estimates[cite: 16].

questions.question: What was the total size of Nepal's very first national budget presented in 2008 BS?
questions.explanation: Nepal's pioneering national budget for the fiscal year 2008 BS amounted to a modest total size of Rs 52.5 million[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which of the following shall have to obtain foreign assistance and borrow loans?
questions.explanation: Under the constitutional arrangement, the Federal Government retains the authority and framework to contract foreign assistance, grants, and international loans[cite: 16].

questions.question: In times of a budget deficit, which of the following is more indicative of a right-wing approach to budgeting?
questions.explanation: Right-wing or conservative fiscal policies generally prefer handling budget shortfalls through borrowing rather than heavy tax hikes on corporations and individuals[cite: 16].

questions.question: In which articles of the present constitution of Nepal, the estimates of revenues and expenditures are included?
questions.explanation: Article 119 of the current Constitution of Nepal mandates the presentation of the annual estimates of revenues and expenditures (the budget)[cite: 16].

questions.question: Arrange the following stages in the enactment of budget in proper order: I. Budget Formulation II. Budget Execution III. Budget Evaluation IV. Budget Formulation [Legislation]
questions.explanation: The proper sequence of the budget cycle starts with formulation (I), proceeds to legislative approval/enactment (IV), followed by execution (II), and concludes with evaluation/audit (III)[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which of the following grants does the Federal Government of Nepal provide to the provincial government and the local body?
questions.explanation: The federal government provides financial transfers comprising fiscal equalization grants, conditional grants, complementary grants, and special grants[cite: 16].

questions.question: Since, when was the budget divides into regular and development in Nepal?
questions.explanation: Nepal initiated the categorization of its national budget into regular and development expenditures starting in F.Y. 2013/14 B.S.[cite: 16].

questions.question: Examine the following statement (s) in the context of Zero Based Budgeting (ZBB). I. It was first proposed by peter A. phyrr. II. It is based on prioritizing all governing expenditure.
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct: Zero-Based Budgeting was pioneered by Peter A. Pyhrr, and it mandates building budgets from a zero base by justifying every single expense[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which of the following is/are the aspects of Sectoral Expenditure of Budget?
questions.explanation: The national budget's expenditure structure is categorized into recurrent expenses, capital investments, and financial management/debt financing[cite: 16].

questions.question: Performance budgeting is based on
questions.explanation: Performance budgeting focuses primarily on the outputs, results, and specific objectives of expenditure rather than merely listing input items[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which of the following is the source of deficit budget?
questions.explanation: Internal borrowing, alongside foreign loans, acts as a primary financing mechanism to cover fiscal deficits when expenditures exceed revenues[cite: 16].

questions.question: Nepal had adopted 'Surplus Budget' in
questions.explanation: Historically, Nepal recorded and adopted a surplus budget during the fiscal year 2033/34 B.S.[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which of the following expenditure is not included in current expenditure?
questions.explanation: Building construction results in physical capital formation, classifying it as a capital expenditure rather than a current/recurrent expense[cite: 16].

questions.question: What measures are adopted to meet the deficit budget?
questions.explanation: Governments cover budget deficits through public debt, drawing foreign loans, and monetary measures such as treasury note issuance[cite: 16].

questions.question: The term 'Programme budgeting' was coined by:
questions.explanation: The conceptual framework and term for program budgeting were introduced and popularized by the Hoover Commission in the United States[cite: 16].

questions.question: Who is regarded as the 'Father of Zero - based budget system'?
questions.explanation: Peter A. Pyhrr is widely recognized as the father and creator of the Zero-Based Budgeting (ZBB) methodology developed in the 1970s[cite: 16].

questions.question: From which country the program budgeting was first introduced?
questions.explanation: Program budgeting was first conceptualized and introduced in the United States government administration[cite: 16].

questions.question: The country at which the Gender Responsive Budget first came to practice in 1984 AD?
questions.explanation: Australia pioneered the adoption and practice of Gender Responsive Budgeting (GRB) in the year 1984 A.D.[cite: 16].

questions.question: How many types of budgets are there based on sectoral expenditure?
questions.explanation: Based on sectoral and functional expenditure allocation, budgets are divided into 3 main categories: Recurrent, Capital, and Financial Provision[cite: 16].

questions.question: Since, when was the budget divides into recurrent expenditure, Capital expenditure & Financial in Nepal?
questions.explanation: The modern tripartite budget classification into recurrent, capital, and financial management was formally implemented in Nepal starting from F.Y. 2061/62 B.S.[cite: 16].

questions.question: A budget in which revenue is equal to expenditure is
questions.explanation: A balanced budget occurs when projected public revenues exactly match total anticipated government expenditures[cite: 16].

questions.question: Nepal has adopted 'programme budgeting' for the first time in?
questions.explanation: Nepal officially integrated and adopted program-based budgeting principles for the first time in FY 2026/27 B.S.[cite: 16].

questions.question: Since when did Nepal start allocating budgets based on prioritization of projects (P1, P2, P3)?
questions.explanation: Project prioritization into P1 (high priority), P2 (medium priority), and P3 (lower priority) categories for budget allocation began in FY 2059/60 BS[cite: 16].

questions.question: Since when has the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) been implemented in Nepal?
questions.explanation: The implementation of the MTEF framework in Nepal's budgetary process was initiated in FY 2059/60[cite: 16].

questions.question: What is the objective of Medium-Term Expenditure Framework (MTEF) linked to the government budgeting system?

options.a: To align annual budgets with periodic plans
options.c: To set standards for public budget translation
options.d: To advise the government on budget spending

questions.explanation: The core objective of the MTEF is to link annual budget allocations systematically with the broader strategic goals of national periodic plans[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which of the following is debt financing?

options.a: Salary paid to the government employees
options.b: Purchase of a machine from Korea
options.c: Repayment of loan taken from the IMF

questions.explanation: Debt servicing expenses such as interest payments on national public debt fall directly under financial management and debt financing[cite: 16].

questions.question: Examine the following statement (s) in the context of Zero Based Budgeting (ZBB). I. It was first taken up in America in the Budget 1970. II. It is based on prioritizing all governing expenditure.
questions.explanation: Both statements are accurate representations of Zero-Based Budgeting, which emerged in US budgeting practice around 1970 and requires complete expenditure prioritization[cite: 16].

questions.question: The government aims to limit the inflation rate to what percentage during the fiscal year 2083/84?
questions.explanation: In recent budgetary targets for FY 2083/84, macroeconomic stabilization policies aim to constrain inflation levels below 6.0%[cite: 16].

questions.question: How much total Amount of budget approximately has been approved by the federal parliament of Nepal for FY 2083/84?
questions.explanation: The total approved volume of the federal budget for FY 2083/84 stands approximately at NPR 2,124.34 billion[cite: 16].

questions.question: Currently FY 2083/84, recurrent budget has been allocated around .......... in the National budget of Nepal.
questions.explanation: Recurrent expenditures constitute approximately 59.80% of the total national budget allocation for FY 2083/84[cite: 16].

questions.question: Currently, Budget speech of FY 2083/84, foreign loan has contributed around .......... in the national budget of Nepal.
questions.explanation: Foreign loans provide approximately 11.64% of the financing sources in the FY 2083/84 national budget framework[cite: 16].

questions.question: What was the actual economic growth at purchaser's price of Nepal's in FY 2081/82?
questions.explanation: Economic performance reports recorded the actual GDP economic growth rate at purchaser's price for FY 2081/82 at 4.43%[cite: 16].

questions.question: How many objectives are there in current budget (FY: 2083/84) of Nepal?
questions.explanation: The current budget for FY 2083/84 outlines 6 core macro-level strategic objectives to steer economic recovery and development[cite: 16].

questions.question: Currently, (FY: 2083/84), foreign grant has contributed around .......... in the national budget of Nepal.
questions.explanation: Foreign grants account for approximately 2.72% of the resource mobilization structure in the FY 2083/84 budget[cite: 16].

questions.question: Currently FY 2083/84, Gender directly Responsive budget has been allocated .......... in the National budget of Nepal.
questions.explanation: The allocation for Gender-Responsive Budgeting (GRB) accounts for 44.30% of the national budget in FY 2083/84[cite: 16].

questions.question: How many government bodies or entities has the budget targeted for abolition, merger or restructuring to trim administrative costs?
questions.explanation: To control administrative expenditures, the budget targeted 55 distinct government entities for structural abolition, merger, or rationalization[cite: 16].

questions.question: Choose correct answer from the following: 1. The budget (FY: 2083/84) has set an ambitious GDP economic growth target of 7.0% Keeping inflation level below 6.0%. 2. First federal budget of Nepal FY 2018/19 was presented on 15th Jestha.
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct under national fiscal records, tracking the 7% growth target / inflation bounds and the debut federal budget date under the current setup[cite: 16].

questions.question: Equalization grants of .......... and .......... to the Province and Local Levels have been allocated respectively for FY 2083/84.
questions.explanation: Fiscal equalization grant allocations for provinces and local levels in FY 2083/84 were set at NPR 61.50 billion and NPR 90.20 billion respectively[cite: 16].

questions.question: According to Financial Procedure and Fiscal Accountability Regulation, 2077 the chairperson of National Resource Estimate Committee is ..........
questions.explanation: The Vice Chairman of the National Planning Commission leads as the chairperson of the National Resource Estimate Committee[cite: 16].

questions.question: On which of the following constitutional bases shall the Government of Nepal Distribute fiscal equalization grants to the Provinces and Local Levels?

options.a: Need of expenditure and population size
options.b: Geographical structure and source of revenue
options.c: Survey of living standard and revenue capacity
options.d: Need of expenditure and revenue capacity

questions.explanation: Constitutional provisions dictate that fiscal equalization grants are distributed based on expenditure needs and internal revenue-raising capacity[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which of the following is primary function of accounting system?
questions.explanation: Recording original financial transactions chronologically in the Journal is the primary foundational function of an accounting system[cite: 16].

questions.question: Who has the authority to approve the format and forms of all government accounting of Nepal?
questions.explanation: The Auditor General of Nepal holds the statutory authority to approve accounting formats and reporting forms across government offices[cite: 16].

questions.question: Who is considered as the father founder of Double Entry Accounting System?
questions.explanation: Italian mathematician Luca Pacioli is globally recognized as the father of the Double-Entry Bookkeeping system[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which one is NOT a feature of New Accounting System?
questions.explanation: Employee recruitment and selection is an HR management function, completely unrelated to the features of the New Government Accounting System[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which of the following is not a characteristic of Nepal's government accounting system?
questions.explanation: Rigid adherence to standardized rules rather than structural flexibility is a characteristic of government accounting; flexibility is thus not a core characteristic[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which of the following is/are not the feature(s) of Government Accounting System?

options.c: Provision of Internal as well as external auditing

questions.explanation: Government accounting focuses on public fund utilization and budgetary compliance, meaning a commercial profit and loss account is not part of its features[cite: 16].

questions.question: New Accounting System based on double entry book-keeping system was introduced in Nepal?
questions.explanation: Nepal officially introduced the New Government Accounting System based on double-entry book-keeping on Chaitra 02, 2018 B.S.[cite: 16].

questions.question: What is the difference between Government Account and commercial Account?
questions.explanation: Government accounts differ from commercial accounts due to their strict reliance on defined budget heads and cash-based accounting principles[cite: 16].

questions.question: When was Laldhadda introduced in Nepal?
questions.explanation: The traditional accounting record ledger system known as 'Laldhadda' was introduced in Nepal in 1871 B.S.[cite: 16].

questions.question: Kitabkhana was established to maintain records of
questions.explanation: Civil Service Records (Kitabkhana) was established specifically to maintain official personnel records of government employees and salary distributions[cite: 16].

questions.question: Laldhadda was introduced to:
questions.explanation: The Laldhadda system was instituted historically to systematically log government revenues and administrative expenses[cite: 16].

questions.question: Who introduced 'Syaha Shrestaa Pranali' in Nepal?
questions.explanation: The traditional 'Syaha Shrestaa Pranali' accounting ledger system was introduced by Kharidaar Gunawanta[cite: 16].

questions.question: Audit independently examines the .......... of the government organization.
questions.explanation: An independent audit verifies financial records to detect and prevent errors, fraud, and financial irregularities or damages[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which of the following is not a principle of final audit?
questions.explanation: While regularity, efficiency, and propriety govern audits, professionalism is treated as a standard norm rather than an exclusive final audit principle in this context, or as outlined in key options[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which is not main objective of auditing?

options.d: to make act, rules and regulation

questions.explanation: Auditing is an examination and verification mechanism; formulating legislative acts, rules, and regulations is the responsibility of parliament and executives, not auditors[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which of the following is not right of an auditor?
questions.explanation: An auditor has rights to examine accounts, vouchers, and request information, but has no legal authority to alter company rules or bylaws[cite: 16].

questions.question: From whom does the approval of the accounting format for recording transactions of a government office come?

options.d: Office of the financial comptroller general office

questions.explanation: The Office of the Auditor General gives final approval to the standardized accounting formats used across government offices[cite: 16].

questions.question: When was Auditor General appointed in Nepal for the first time?
questions.explanation: The first Auditor General of Nepal was appointed on Ashadh 15, 2016 B.S.[cite: 16].

questions.question: When was office of financial comptroller general office (FCGO) established for the first time in Nepal?
questions.explanation: The Financial Comptroller General Office (FCGO) was established in 2032 B.S. to manage government accounting and payment systems[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which of the following element(s) are considered while doing internal audit?
questions.explanation: Internal auditing examines financial transactions for regulatory compliance, administrative propriety, and operational efficiency[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which agency prepares national financial statement of the government of Nepal?

options.b: Office of the financial comptroller general office

questions.explanation: The Financial Comptroller General Office (FCGO) is responsible for compiling and preparing the consolidated national financial statements of the government[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which entity is liable for final Audit of Accounts of Government of Nepal?

options.b: Office of the financial comptroller general office

questions.explanation: The Office of the Auditor General conducts the final statutory external audit of all government accounts in Nepal[cite: 16].

questions.question: What is the role of the auditor general in the government's accounting and audit system in Nepal?

options.a: To ensure that government resources are used in accordance with the approved budget
options.b: To ensure that the accounts of the government are maintained in a proper and efficient manner
options.c: To ensure that the financial statements of the government present a true picture

questions.explanation: The Auditor General ensures proper budget utilization, accurate accounting maintenance, and true financial statement reporting[cite: 16].

questions.question: In the context of Nepali Government System, what is the full form of CGAS?
questions.explanation: CGAS stands for Computerized Government Accounting System, deployed to modernize government bookkeeping and reporting[cite: 16].

questions.question: Auditor general is appointed by?
questions.explanation: In accordance with the constitution, the President of Nepal appoints the Auditor General upon the recommendation of the Constitutional Council[cite: 16].

questions.question: The reports of the Comptroller and Auditor-General of Nepal relating to the accounts of the Provinces are submitted to which among the following?
questions.explanation: Auditor General reports regarding federal and provincial accounts are submitted to the President of Nepal, who subsequently causes them to be laid before federal/provincial legislatures[cite: 16].

questions.question: Under which article of the constitution of Nepal are the functions, duties and power of Auditor General mentioned?
questions.explanation: Article 241 of the Constitution of Nepal explicitly details the functions, duties, and powers of the Auditor General[cite: 16].

questions.question: Government auditing is concerned with:
questions.explanation: Government auditing heavily centers around the systematic verification of financial records, vouchers, and compliance[cite: 16].

questions.question: International Auditing Standards are issued by

options.c: International Audit and Assurance Standards Board

questions.explanation: International Standards on Auditing are promulgated by the International Auditing and Assurance Standards Board (IAASB)[cite: 16].

questions.question: Which of the following is/are features of internal audit?
questions.explanation: Effective internal audit reports and procedures require objectivity, clarity, and concise brevity in communicating findings[cite: 16].

questions.question: What does 'GFS' stand for in government accounting?
questions.explanation: GFS stands for Government Finance Statistics, an international statistical framework used to analyze government financial operations[cite: 16].
